speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your follow-up visit. I understand you are experiencing occasional shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after your tympanoplasty. To better understand your condition, have you noticed any drainage, fever, or changes in hearing since the surgery?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your history of chronic ear infections and the timing of your surgery, the shooting pain when eating suggests possible Eustachian tube dysfunction. Have you noticed any fullness or popping in your right ear during swallowing, and does the pain radiate to your jaw or neck?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: The shooting pain triggered by eating and the discomfort with earrings point toward a specific complication involving your ear canal or nerve. Have you noticed any redness, swelling, or discharge coming from the ear canal, and does the pain feel like a deep ache rather than surface-level? REQUEST TEST: Otoscopy.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Post-Tympanoplasty Granuloma (specifically Granulation Tissue) with associated Auriculotemporal Neuralgia.

The "shooting pain with eating" indicates nerve involvement (Auriculotemporal neuralgia), while the discomfort with earrings and history of chronic infections suggest a vascularized lesion like a granuloma in the ear canal. The otoscopy report excluded active infection, supporting a benign proliferative complication rather than Tuberculosis.
